_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); automaker signals, the early era

pit_profile.why: Ford Motor Company: 'We are one of the world’s largest producers of cars and trucks.' ('As of December 31, 2009, our vehicle brands included Ford, Mercury, Lincoln, and Volvo, although Volvo is held for sale.'); among its risk factors, 'Further declines in industry sales volume, particularly in the United States or Europe, due to financial crisis, deepening recession, geo-political events, or other factors.' and 'An increase in or acceleration of market shift beyond our current planning assumptions from sales of trucks, medium- and large-sized utilities, or other more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States.'; 'Further, the automotive industry is a highly competitive, cyclical business that has a wide and growing variety of product offerings from a growing number of manufacturers.' (the industry, not the company's own earnings, is called cyclical: DURABLE, the AVGO precedent) (its own FY2009 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an automaker on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on the shift away from trucks and SUVs stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

(the industry, not the company's own earnings, is called cyclical: DURABLE, the AVGO precedent) (its own FY2009 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an automaker on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on the shift away from trucks and SUVs stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.95x; +47% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.35; conservative 2yr +39%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -52.6%/yr (worst year FY02-FY05, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +21.4%/yr (Q1 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 8.5-yr ex-FY06 ex-FY07 ex-FY08 ex-FY09 median

BULL.desc: EPS +21.4%/yr (FY02-FY05 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +94.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY05); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: F (retrospective, 2010-07-02) ◎ ACCUMULATE — Ratio B 0.95x (90.3% downside to Bear $1 / +94.6% upside to Bull $20) | Adj composite 3.12 vs market 1.77: gap +1.35 [UNDERVALUED] | +47% above the EPP floor $7 (7x FY10E $1.00) | Conservative 2-yr case: +38.6% total (+19.3%/yr) | At 10.3x FY10E the 15% hurdle price $14 sits at or below the BASE case; wholesale units +27.1% in Q1 2010, forward revenues +29.5% (no Q2 2010 revenue guide, Q1 2010 revenue as reported); no disruption theme is live for an automaker on this date.
